research_notes: Comprehensive research for France Travel Scams book. Bordeaux is generally a safe city compared to Paris or Marseille, but pickpocketing and tourist scams remain concerns. Sources include UK FCDO France Travel Advice, US Embassy France, TravelSafe Abroad, World Nomads, Tripadvisor forums, and local French news.

scams.location: Place de la Bourse, Rue Sainte-Catherine, Miroir d'Eau, tourist landmarks
scams.story: Pickpockets operate in crowded tourist areas throughout Bordeaux, particularly at Place de la Bourse, along Rue Sainte-Catherine (one of Europe's longest pedestrian shopping streets), and near the Miroir d'Eau. Thieves work in teams, using distraction techniques while accomplices steal wallets, phones, and valuables. They often target tourists who are taking photos or consulting maps.
red_flags: Groups of people suddenly crowding around you
Someone bumping into you unnecessarily in an uncrowded area
People watching you take out your wallet or phone
Strangers offering unsolicited help with directions
how_to_avoid: Use anti-theft bags with hidden compartments
Keep wallets in front pockets, never back pockets
Avoid displaying expensive jewelry or electronics
Stay alert in crowded areas
Keep bags zipped and in front of your body

scams.location: Gare de Bordeaux Saint-Jean, train platforms, ticket areas
scams.story: Bordeaux Saint-Jean train station attracts pickpockets who target confused tourists carrying luggage. A common tactic involves groups of 4-6 people pushing onto trains just before doors close, crowding targets while accomplices steal valuables, then hopping off as doors close. Thieves also operate near ticket machines and in crowded platform areas.
red_flags: Groups rushing onto trains at the last second
People crowding you unnecessarily near train doors
Someone distracting you while others stand too close
Offers of help with ticket machines from strangers
how_to_avoid: Keep bags in front of you and secured at all times
Be extra vigilant when boarding trains
Don't put phones or wallets in easily accessible pockets
Watch for people crowding you unnecessarily
Board trains early rather than rushing at the last moment

scams.location: Tourist areas, near monuments, pedestrian zones
scams.story: Scammers approach tourists with clipboards asking them to sign a petition, often claiming to support deaf children or a charitable cause. While the tourist is distracted reading and signing, an accomplice steals their wallet, phone, or valuables from bags or pockets. Sometimes the petitioner themselves will demand a donation after signing, becoming aggressive if refused.
red_flags: Clipboard petitioners in English (a red flag in France)
Person claiming to be deaf-mute
Multiple people with clipboards working the same area
Request for immediate cash donation after signing
how_to_avoid: Politely decline and keep walking
Never stop for clipboard solicitors
Keep hands on your belongings
Say 'non merci' firmly while continuing to move
Never sign anything on the street

scams.location: Tourist areas, near cafes and restaurants, pedestrian zones
scams.story: A stranger approaches and begins tying a colorful string bracelet on your wrist as a supposed 'gift' or sign of friendship. Once the bracelet is tied, they aggressively demand payment, often 10-20 euros. They refuse to take the bracelet back and may create a scene to pressure payment. Meanwhile, accomplices may use the distraction to pickpocket you.
red_flags: Someone approaching with colored string or yarn
Attempts to touch your hand or wrist
Overly friendly strangers offering free gifts
Groups working together near tourist areas
how_to_avoid: Keep your hands in your pockets or crossed
Firmly refuse any 'gifts' from strangers
Say 'non' and walk away quickly
Never let strangers touch your hands or wrists
If a bracelet is tied, refuse to pay and walk toward police

scams.location: Near tourist attractions, parks, riverside walkways
scams.story: A scammer pretends to 'find' a gold ring on the ground near you and insists you should have it, claiming it doesn't fit them or suggesting you can sell it. They then ask for a small finder's fee or payment. The ring is worthless brass or fake gold. This scam is particularly common throughout France and targets tourists who appear kind or confused.
red_flags: Someone dramatically 'finding' jewelry near you
Insistence that you should have this 'lucky find'
The ring appears too shiny for something found on the street
Sob story following the discovery
how_to_avoid: Ignore anyone who approaches with a 'found' ring
Keep walking without engaging
Say 'Ce n'est pas à moi' (It's not mine) and walk away
Remember that real gold rings are never given away by strangers

scams.location: Tourist areas, metro stations, busy streets
scams.story: Scammers posing as plainclothes police officers flash fake badges and demand to inspect your wallet for 'counterfeit currency.' They work in pairs: one may pretend to be a drug dealer to engage you, then the fake officer appears to 'investigate.' While examining your cash, they palm bills. Real French police never ask to see your wallet contents on the street.
red_flags: Plainclothes officers without uniformed backup
Quick flash of badge without proper identification
Request to see your wallet rather than ID
A 'tourist' accomplice who engaged you just before
Refusal to go to a police station
how_to_avoid: Real police only ask to see ID documents, not wallets
Request to see official identification clearly
Insist on going to the nearest police station
Call 17 (police) if uncertain
Never hand over your wallet to anyone on the street

scams.location: Bordeaux-Merignac Airport, Gare Saint-Jean train station
scams.story: Unlicensed taxi drivers approach tourists at Bordeaux-Merignac Airport or Gare Saint-Jean, offering rides at inflated prices. They may claim there's a taxi strike or that official taxis are unavailable. These unofficial drivers can charge 2-3 times the normal fare and may not be insured. Some use rigged meters or claim the meter is broken.
red_flags: Drivers approaching you rather than waiting at official ranks
Claims of taxi strikes or unavailable official taxis
No visible taxi signage or luminous roof sign
Refusal to use meter or quoting flat rates
how_to_avoid: Only use taxis from official taxi ranks
Look for vehicles with official taxi signage and roof lights
Use ride-sharing apps like Uber or Bolt for transparent pricing
Always confirm the fare before getting in
Note the driver's license number displayed in the vehicle

scams.location: Tourist areas, restaurants near major attractions
scams.story: Some restaurants in tourist areas show tourists different menus with higher prices, add hidden charges for bread, water, or table settings, or charge for items not ordered. Staff may also substitute cheaper wine when premium glasses are ordered. Bills may include undisclosed service charges or inflated prices for tourists, especially Americans.
red_flags: Menus without prices displayed outside
Different menus for different customers
Aggressive insistence on specials without prices
Items appearing on bill that weren't ordered
how_to_avoid: Check that menus display prices (legally required in France)
Compare printed menu prices to your bill
Ask 'une carafe d'eau' for free tap water
Verify wine bottle labels match what you ordered
Avoid restaurants without posted prices

scams.location: Tourist areas, train stations, shopping districts
scams.story: Criminals install skimming devices on ATMs to capture card details and PINs. These devices blend with the ATM's original hardware and are hard to detect. Scammers also use distraction techniques: one person engages you while another watches you enter your PIN or manipulates the machine to trap your card.
red_flags: ATM card slots that appear loose or unusual
Extra attachments near the keypad
Strangers offering to help at ATMs
Your card getting stuck in the machine
how_to_avoid: Use ATMs inside banks during business hours
Inspect card slots for loose attachments
Cover keypad when entering PIN
Never accept help from strangers at ATMs
If card is trapped, don't leave and call your bank immediately

scams.location: Restaurant terraces, outdoor cafes, riverside areas, romantic spots
scams.story: Men approach couples or women at restaurant terraces and outdoor cafes, offering a 'free' rose as a romantic gesture. Once the rose is accepted or touched, they aggressively demand payment of 5-10 euros. They refuse to take the rose back and create uncomfortable confrontations. Sometimes accomplices use this distraction to pickpocket victims.
red_flags: Sellers approaching dining couples specifically
Insistence that the rose is 'free' or a 'gift'
Placing the rose in your hand before you agree
Aggressive behavior when payment is refused
how_to_avoid: Decline firmly and keep your hands away
Avoid touching offered items
Say 'non merci' without stopping
Alert restaurant staff if sellers become aggressive

scams.location: Bordeaux tram lines, buses, stops near tourist attractions
scams.story: Pickpockets operate on Bordeaux's tram network and buses, particularly during rush hours and on routes serving tourist areas. Thieves create distractions by bumping into victims or 'helping' with bags while accomplices steal valuables. At stops near tourist destinations, thieves may grab phones or bags just as doors are closing.
red_flags: People standing unusually close on uncrowded trams
Groups boarding just before doors close
Someone bumping into you or creating a commotion
Offers of unsolicited help with bags or directions
how_to_avoid: Keep valuables in front pockets or secure inside bags
Stay alert especially near doors
Be wary of anyone offering unsolicited help
Avoid standing near doors with easily accessible items

scams.location: Online booking platforms, social media advertisements
scams.story: Scammers create fake Airbnb or rental listings using photos from legitimate properties, offering attractive prices in desirable locations. They request payment via wire transfer or cryptocurrency outside the official platform, then disappear. Tourists arrive to find the property doesn't exist or belongs to someone else. France is a hotspot for this scam.
red_flags: Prices significantly below market rate
Requests to communicate off-platform
Payment requested via wire transfer or cryptocurrency
Pressure to pay quickly
No reviews or very few reviews
how_to_avoid: Only book through official platforms and pay through their systems
Be suspicious of unusually low prices
Never wire money directly
Verify listings have reviews and host history
Use Google Street View to verify property exists
